text.p: Stratosphere Corp., operator of the Stratosphere hotel-casino in Las Vegas, said Thurdsay it does not plan to make an interest payment due next month on mortgage notes and will probably file for bankruptcy.
Stratosphere also reported a much wider loss for the third quarter.
The Las Vegas-based company, which has struggled since opening on April 30, is negotiating with creditors to amend terms of its $203 million of 14.25 percent first mortgage notes.
"It is highly likely that negotations with its creditors, whether successful or not at arriving at a restructuring, will involve a bankruptcy filing," the company said in a statement.

Ever since it opened, Stratosphere has suffered from room rates that were too high and a poorly planned casino, industry analysts said. The company has slashed rates, re-configured its casino floor and revamped its marketing plan.
It unveiled its new casino design on Oct. 1, and in the first three weeks of October generated $5.7 million in gambling revenue, up 68.5 percent from the same period in September.
It also said it lost $26 million, or 45 cents a share, in the third quarter, compared with a loss of $2.3 million, or 6 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.

The company said current cash projections lead it to believe it will not make the $15 million interest payment due on Nov. 15. It was also trying to restructure capital lease obligations and was evaluating whether it can meet an Oct. 30 payment.
Grand Casinos Inc., which owns and operates hotel-casino properties in several states, owns 42 percent of Stratosphere.
